content: 1. A systematic review and meta-analysis was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2016, volume 16, issue 11, pages 1269–1278. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) released the second edition of its consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection in 2016, providing recommendations for a public health approach. 3. Spyridis NP and colleagues conducted an 11-year randomized study comparing the effectiveness of a 9-month regimen of isoniazid alone versus 3and 4-month regimens of isoniazid plus rifampin for treating latent tuberculosis infection in children. The results were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2007, volume 45, issue 6, pages 715–722. 4. The WHO published updated and consolidated guidelines for the programmatic management of latent tuberculosis infection, including Annex 2, which contains evidence-to-decision and GRADE tables. 5. Galli L and colleagues analyzed epidemiological and clinical data on pediatric tuberculosis in Italian children, based on the Italian Register of Pediatric Tuberculosis. Their findings were published in International Journal of Molecular Sciences in 2016, volume 17, issue 6. 6. Van Zyl S and colleagues studied adherence to anti-tuberculosis chemoprophylaxis and treatment in children, with their findings published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2006, volume 10, issue 1, pages 13–18. 7. Stagg HR and colleagues conducted a network meta-analysis on the treatment of latent tuberculosis infection, published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2014, volume 161, issue 6, pages 419–428. 8. Shepardson D and MacKenzie WR provided an update on the cost-effectiveness of a 12-dose regimen for latent tuberculosis infection at new rifapentine prices, published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2014, volume 18, issue 6, page 751. 9. Martinson NA and colleagues evaluated new regimens to prevent tuberculosis in adults with HIV infection, with their study published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2011, volume 365, issue 1, pages 11–20. 10. Sterling TR and colleagues investigated the use of a 3-month weekly regimen of rifapentine and isoniazid for treating Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection in HIV-coinfected individuals. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2016, volume 30, issue 10, pages 1607–1615. 11. Sterling TR, Villarino ME, and colleagues studied a 3-month regimen of rifapentine and isoniazid for latent tuberculosis infection, with results published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2011, volume 365, issue 23, pages 2155–2166. 12. Villarino ME and colleagues conducted a randomized clinical trial on a 3-month, 12-dose regimen of rifapentine and isoniazid for preventing tuberculosis in children and adolescents. The study was published in JAMA Pediatrics in 2015, volume 169, issue 3, pages 247–255. 13. The WHO released the Global Tuberculosis Report in 2016, providing comprehensive data on the global TB epidemic. 14. Schaaf HS and colleagues reviewed recent developments in managing multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in children, with their findings published in Current Opinion in Infectious Diseases in 2014, volume 27, issue 3, pages 211–219. 15. Bamrah S and colleagues reported on the treatment of latent tuberculosis infection in contacts of multidrug-resistant TB patients in the Federated States of Micronesia from 2009 to 2012. The study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2014, volume 18, issue 8, pages 912–918. 16. Garcia-Prats AJ and colleagues conducted a contact investigation of children exposed to multidrug-resistant tuberculosis at a home-based daycare center. Their findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2014, volume 18, issue 11, pages 1292–1298. 17. Trieu L, Proops DC, and Ahuja SD studied the use of moxifloxacin prophylaxis against multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in New York, USA. Their findings were published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2015, volume 21, issue 3, pages 500–503. 18. Fox GJ and colleagues reviewed strategies for preventing the spread of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis and protecting contacts of infectious cases. Their work was published in Clinical Microbiology and Infection in 2017, volume 23, issue 3, pages 147–153. 19. The American Thoracic Society published recommendations on targeted tuberculin testing and treatment of latent tuberculosis infection in MMWR Recommendations and Reports in 2000, volume 49, issue RR-6, pages 1–51. 20. Cain KP, Nelson LJ, and Cegielski JP reviewed global policies and practices for managing individuals exposed to multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Their findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2010, volume 14, issue 3, pages 269–274. 21. The WHO published a companion handbook to its guidelines for the programmatic management of drug-resistant tuberculosis in 2014. 22. The WHO released a framework for implementing active TB drug-safety monitoring and management (aDSM) in 2015. 23. Kritski AL and colleagues studied the transmission of tuberculosis to close contacts of patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Their findings were published in American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 1996, volume 153, issue 1, pages 331–335.
